name: Swiss cheese plant
light_needs: Moderate brightness, not direct sunlight. NC State also lists partial shade.
water_guidance: Water thoroughly, then allow the top quarter to one-third of the mix to dry before watering again. No day count is published.
description: NC State describes low-severity poisoning from needle-like calcium oxalate crystals: intense burning of the mouth, tongue, and throat if eaten, and skin irritation from the sap. ASPCA lists Monstera deliciosa as toxic to dogs and cats for the same principle.
common_problems: Root rot from soil that stays wet
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/monstera-deliciosa/ (retrieved 2026-11-09). Pet listing: ASPCA, https://www.aspca.org/pet-care/aspca-poison-control/toxic-and-non-toxic-plants/cutleaf-philodendron (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Snake plant
light_needs: Direct sun only part of the day (2 to 6 hours). NC State says it also tolerates very low light.
water_guidance: In spring to autumn, allow the soil to dry between waterings. In winter, water only every one to two months. The winter phrase is a range, so no single day count is stored.
description: NC State: toxic if ingested because of saponins. Symptoms listed include vomiting, depression, nausea, diarrhea, anorexia, hypersalivation, and dilated pupils in cats. The sap can irritate skin. Tagged as a problem for children, cats, and dogs.
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/dracaena-trifasciata/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Fiddle-leaf fig
light_needs: Bright indirect light or partial shade, with protection from afternoon sun.
water_guidance: NC State says this plant prefers moist, well-drained soil and is sensitive to overwatering. It does not publish a number of days between waterings.
description: NC State: toxic to humans, cats, and dogs if ingested. Listed effects include oral irritation, excessive drooling, and vomiting. The milky sap can irritate skin. Keep temperatures greater than 55 F (13 C).
common_problems: Leaf drop from too much or too little water
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/ficus-lyrata/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Golden pothos
light_needs: Bright indirect light. NC State says it survives for long periods in low light, and low light can fade variegation.
water_guidance: Let the well-drained potting medium dry out between waterings. No day count is published.
description: NC State lists medium-severity poisoning from calcium oxalate crystals: oral irritation, swelling, drooling, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, skin irritation, and diarrhea. Tagged as a problem for cats and dogs.
common_problems: Root rot and black leaf margins from overwatering
Loss of variegation in low light
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/epipremnum-aureum/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: ZZ plant
light_needs: Bright indirect sunlight. NC State says it grows in very low light, and direct sun can scald and brown the leaves.
water_guidance: Summer: water twice monthly, and only if the soil has dried completely. Winter: water once a month while it is not actively growing. The stored 14-day interval is only the summer phrase "twice monthly."
description: NC State: medium toxicity. Calcium oxalate; diarrhea and vomiting if leaves are consumed in quantity. Tagged as a problem for cats and dogs. Direct sun can scald the leaves.
common_problems: Rot if the soil stays wet
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/zamioculcas-zamiifolia/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Aloe vera
water_guidance: Allow the soil to dry completely between waterings, and water less often in winter. No day count is published.
description: NC State: low-severity poisoning through ingestion or skin contact with the latex. Symptoms listed include abdominal cramping, diarrhea, red urine, and skin irritation. Tagged as a problem for cats, dogs, and horses. The inner gel is a separate preparation and is not a reason to eat the leaf.
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/aloe-vera/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Peace lily
light_needs: Partial to deep shade. Do not place it in direct sun.
water_guidance: Keep the soil moist but not soggy, and allow it to dry between waterings. No day count is published. Day temperatures cited as 68 to 85 F.
description: NC State: medium-severity poisoning from calcium oxalate crystals if leaves are eaten in quantity. Symptoms include severe mouth pain, a burning sensation, drooling, vomiting, and difficulty swallowing. Tagged as a problem for children, cats, and dogs.
common_problems: Brown leaf tips from direct sun, underwatering, or low humidity
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/spathiphyllum/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Peacock plant
light_needs: Bright indirect sun or partial shade. Direct sun can burn the leaves.
water_guidance: Keep the mix moist but not wet or soggy, and decrease watering in winter. No day count is published. NC State recommends distilled or rain water because fluoride in tap water can brown the leaves.
description: NC State tags this plant non-toxic for cats, dogs, and horses. The page does not list it as poisonous to people. Temperatures cited as 65 to 75 F.
common_problems: Leaf roll or browning in low humidity
Leaf browning from fluoridated tap water
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/goeppertia-makoyana/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Spider plant
light_needs: Medium light. It tolerates deep shade and is intolerant of direct sunlight.
water_guidance: It grows best in moist soil and is also described as tolerant of drought. Reduce watering in winter. No day count is published. NC State says chlorine and fluoride in tap water can burn leaf tips.
description: NC State tags Chlorophytum comosum non-toxic for cats, dogs, and horses. The page does not list a human poison section. Keep temperatures above 45 F (7 C).
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/chlorophytum-comosum/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Boston fern
water_guidance: Keep the soil moist and do not let it dry out. Reduce watering in winter, when overwatering can lead to root rot. No day count is published.
description: NC State tags Nephrolepis exaltata non-toxic for cats, dogs, and horses. The page does not list a human poison section. Cited indoor temperatures are 60 to 70 F. Dark dots on the frond undersides can be spores rather than insects.
common_problems: Scale or spider mites when the air is dry
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/nephrolepis-exaltata/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Rubber plant
light_needs: Bright indirect light or partial shade, with protection from afternoon sun.
water_guidance: Water regularly and avoid overwatering. Reduce watering from fall to late winter while the plant is dormant. No day count is published.
description: NC State tags Ficus elastica as a problem for cats, dogs, and horses. This seed does not mark it poisonous to people because that page's problem list does not include a human-poison section. Cut leaves drip sap. Keep temperatures greater than 55 F (13 C).
common_problems: Leaf loss from overwatering, cold, or drafts
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/ficus-elastica/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).

name: Jade plant
light_needs: A sunny indoor spot that also has some afternoon shade.
water_guidance: Water in moderation when the soil is dry, and reduce watering from fall to late winter. No day count is published.
description: NC State tags Crassula ovata as a problem for cats, dogs, and horses. This seed does not mark it poisonous to people because that page does not include a human-poison section. Leaf fall and root rot can follow overwatering.
common_problems: Root rot and leaf fall from overwatering
care_source: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/crassula-ovata/ (retrieved 2026-11-09).
